Saint-Gobain Reports Steady Trade Volumes Amidst Stable French Construction Sector

Cie de Saint-Gobain SA, a leading player in France’s construction materials industry, reported routine trade volumes for the second quarter, reflecting ongoing stability in the sector. According to figures released on Wednesday, the company’s shipments of glass, insulation, and building solutions remained in line with seasonal expectations, showing modest growth compared to the same period last year.

The company’s quarterly report indicated that domestic demand continues to be supported by public infrastructure projects and residential renovation programs. “Our trade volumes this quarter are consistent with our forecasts and reflect the resilience of the French construction market,” said Luc Morel, Saint-Gobain’s Director of Investor Relations. He noted that steady order flows from both private and public sector clients have helped maintain output levels across the company’s production sites.

The French Construction Materials Association noted similar trends across the industry. “We are seeing stable activity throughout the sector, with no significant disruptions or supply chain constraints,” said Marie Fournier, a spokesperson for the group. “Saint-Gobain’s latest figures underscore the industry’s adaptability in the current macroeconomic environment.”

Analysts at Paris-based brokerage Durand & Fils commented that Saint-Gobain’s steady performance aligns with their expectations for the broader construction materials market in France. “The company is benefiting from consistent domestic demand and a relatively predictable regulatory landscape,” said analyst Etienne Lefevre.

Exports of construction materials from France also remained stable, with Saint-Gobain’s shipments to neighboring European markets unchanged from last quarter. Employment levels and production rates at the company’s facilities were reported to be normal, with no disruptions or changes in operating schedules.

Looking ahead, Saint-Gobain said it expects trade activity to remain within historical ranges for the remainder of the year, barring any unforeseen developments.
